newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Russia's Lebed cautions NATO on expansion.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Lebed cautions NATO on expansion.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed, on his first visit to the West, said after talks with NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana on Monday that the alliance should approach any eastward expansion with extreme caution.

"Every step must be calculated. Take stock, take stock and take stock again," he told reporters after talks at NATO's Brussels headquarters. But he appeared to leave open the possibility of an arrangement.
Asked if he had heard any new initiatives from Solana during his first round of talks, he replied: "Nothing."

"I came to say let's work together, let's solve the problem...of modernising, reforming NATO, the establishment of special, as we say, relations between Russia and NATO, expressed in an agreement or treaty with legal status and then, further, take a decision on expansion or non-expansion," he said.
"We're building a collective security, not security for individuals."
The Russian foreign ministry has taken a more accommodating approach to the NATO plan in recent weeks, seeking security guarantees over any expansion.

However, Lebed, President Boris Yeltsin's security adviser, has remained a vociferous opponent of plans for the 16-nation alliance to incorporate some former members of the now defunct Soviet-led Warsaw Pact alliance.
He once accused the alliance of behaving like a drunken hooligan in a kindergarten over its plans and only last week said expansion could bring a return to Cold War-style hostility.
Lebed said he had new proposals on solving the dispute but did not have time to present them to Solana. These would be discussed at a meeting later on Monday with NATO ambassadors.
